newsitem.title: USA: USDA revs up world centrif. sugar output estimate.
newsitem.headline: USDA revs up world centrif. sugar output estimate.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Thursday said it revised its forecast for 1996/97 world centrifugal sugar production to 121.4 million tonnes, up from a preliminary estimate of 120.2 million tonnes in May.
USDA pegged India's output in 1996/97 at 15.0 million tonnes, up from 14.1 million seen in May, but down from a record outturn of 18.2 million in 1995/96.
It estimated Brazil sugar production at 14.2 million tonnes, up from 14.0 million previously forecast and left the China output estimate unchanged at 6.6 million tonnes.

USDA pinned the record 1996/97 Brazil sugar output forecast on favorable weather, increased cane production as the industry recovers from the 1994 frost, and the conversion of alcohol distilleries into sugar mills capable of producing both sugar and alcohol.

USDA revised up its output forecast for Cuba to 4.6 million tonnes from 4.2 million tonnes seen in May, citing the continuation of outside financing for inputs and equipment and the implementation of economic reforms.

The department lowered its forecast for European Union 1996/97 sugar production to 16.7 million tonnes from 17.2 million estimated in May and down from last season's outturn of 17 million tonnes. It revised down output estimates for Italy and France citing weather.

USDA cut its estimate for Ukranian 1996/97 sugar output to 2.7 million tonnes from May's 3.7 million forecast due to freezing weather during the spring and hot, dry weather during the early summer months. It said the situation was further aggravated by input and requirement shortages.
The department also lowered its estimate for Russia 1996/97 sugar production to 1.95 million tonnes from 2.1 million tonnes forecast in May.
